blockers.title: EV-3 retains 'the verified tree digest' as required evidence, but schemas.v11 makes a single tree-root digest a RESERVED BINDING POINT whose population is RJ-6, parked on DR-006's freeze §7.1 identity recipe that this same file refuses to invent
blockers.finding: EV-3's retained list opens: 'Once authored: per D-002 platform (...), the verified tree digest, the held descriptor or open-handle identity or digest-recheck record from verification through spawn (the digest recheck is tree-scoped: ... rechecked against the signed TreeCommitment), ...'. A single digest OF the verified tree is a named, reserved, refused identity in the law this file consumes. component-manifest-schemas.v11 — cited here at a digest I reproduced — carries the feature 'Single-root tree commitment (treeRootDigest)' with ridesOn 'DR-006/the identity-recipe property: a minted Merkle-style root is a derived identity requiring a producing recipe; the corpus records typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot as exactly this class with no rule' and consequence 'treeRootDigest stays a RESERVED BINDING POINT; populating it before its recipe closes is RJ-6.' Its RJ-6 trigger names treeRootDigest in the reserved list and states 'reserved means reserved'. Its TreeCommitment semantics says the same thing positively: 'This schema deliberately does NOT mint a single tree-root digest.' DR-006's live row is 'Freeze §7.1 identity-recipe property and exact FACT-PLANE closure items remain open', so the recipe that would make a tree digest producible is the §7.1 recipe — the one this cycle's dispatch forbids inventing and the one this file's own doesNot refuses at entry 14, 'Does not invent a section 7.1 recipe.' So EV-3 requires a fixture to retain an artifact that is, under the file's own consumed law, either a reserved-field population typed RJ-6 or a derived identity awaiting a parked recipe. The generous reading is that 'the verified tree digest' is loose wording for the TreeCommitment entry set. Two things cut against leaving it to the reader. The file is precise everywhere else it means per-entry — EV-1 says 'the extracted tree as path/type/mode/length/digest' and 'Each extracted file sha256 equals the signed TreeCommitment entry', and EV-3's own next clause says 'rechecked against the signed TreeCommitment' — so the singular 'digest' stands out as a distinct retained item, listed separately from the recheck record. And a single value to compare at spawn is exactly what a harness author would want here, which is why schemas.v11 troubled to reject it and to record typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot as the cautionary instance of a root digest with no producing rule. The trap is baited precisely where this member sits.
blockers.provenance: This phrase is not a v2 regression. It is byte-identical in v1, appears once in each file, and I did not catch it at turn 1. The v2 repair to the surrounding sentence is what made it visible: once EV-3 states the recheck is tree-scoped against the signed TreeCommitment, the separately retained singular tree digest has nothing left to be except the reserved identity. I record this as my miss, not as the author's backslide.
blockers.whyItMatters: The next act on this line is fixture authoring. A fixture author following this specification literally either produces a tree-root digest — populating a reserved binding point, RJ-6, against law recorded at D-104 — or stalls on a DR-006 recipe that is open and that no one in this cycle may write. An exact-byte specification exists to prevent exactly that fork.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Delete the phrase, or replace it with the per-entry form the rest of the file uses — the signed TreeCommitment entry set for the platform under test. The recheck clause already carries the binding work, so nothing else in EV-3 changes. If the author genuinely wants a single comparison value, that is not a harness-specification decision: it is DR-006 / freeze §7.1, and it must not be minted here.
